title: Non-blocking finding from PR #346's review (frontend-ibkr-login-button-followups-followups-followups)
description: Tracked follow-up for a non-blocking finding raised in pr-reviewer's `code-review` pass on PR #346 (frontend-ibkr-login-button-followups-followups-followups) -- does not block the accept (speculative, very low-probability edge case, not reproduced against any real browser or in the test suite), but worth fixing/considering so it isn't lost once PR #346 merges and the review comment disappears from view.

checklist.step: PR #346 moved `window.addEventListener('blur', handleBlurAfterClick)` (and the `pendingBlurListenerRef.current = handleBlurAfterClick` assignment) in `IbkrStatusIndicator.tsx`'s login button `onClick` handler to immediately *before* `window.open(login_url, '_blank', 'noopener,noreferrer')`, closing a narrow timing gap (see that task's checklist). One side effect of that reordering: if `window.open` were ever to throw synchronously (most browsers just silently no-op/return `null` for a popup-blocked or malformed-scheme URL rather than throwing, but some environments do throw for a disallowed scheme), the click handler would now throw *after* the `blur` listener is already registered, so `cooldownTimeoutRef` is never set and the listener is never cleaned up via `window.removeEventListener` -- it would stay registered until the component unmounts (a `pendingBlurListenerRef.current` leak). Before PR #346's reorder, that same synchronous-throw path never reached the `addEventListener` call at all, so no stray listener existed in that failure path. `isOpeningLogin` staying stuck `true` on that path is a pre-existing, already-accepted risk (unchanged by this PR); only the added dangling-listener side effect is new. Consider wrapping the `window.open(...)` call in a `try/catch` (or a `try/finally` that always clears the listener + ref) so a synchronous throw from `window.open` can't leave `pendingBlurListenerRef.current` pointing at a listener nothing will ever remove. Low likelihood, not reproduced in any real browser or in the test suite -- worth a deliberate look rather than losing it as a review-comment-only note.

decisions.decision: Wrapped only the `window.open(login_url, '_blank', 'noopener,noreferrer')` call itself in a `try { ... } catch (err) { ...cleanup...; throw err }`, rather than a `try/finally` around a larger block or swallowing the error. On a synchronous throw, the `catch` removes the just-registered `blur` listener and clears `pendingBlurListenerRef.current`, then rethrows the original error unchanged.
decisions.rationale: Rethrowing (rather than swallowing) keeps this fix scoped exactly to the dangling-listener side effect the checklist item describes, leaving the pre-existing, already-accepted `isOpeningLogin` stuck-`true` failure mode on the same path completely untouched -- swallowing the error would have silently changed that other behavior too (e.g. by letting execution reach the `cooldownTimeoutRef` assignment below, which the checklist explicitly says is out of scope). Rejected a broader `try/finally` around the whole click handler body: `finally` would run its cleanup unconditionally even on the non-throwing success path, and the existing code already has its own correct, more precise cleanup for that path (the `cooldownTimeoutRef` timeout and the unmount effect) -- adding a second, redundant cleanup path there would just be more surface area for the two to disagree. Verified with a mutation test: reverted just the `try/catch` (restoring the bare `window.open(...)` call, leaving the new test in `IbkrStatusIndicator.test.tsx` untouched) and reran the file's suite -- the new test failed with the `removeEventListener` mock recording `['error', ...]` as its only call instead of `['blur', handlerFn]` (confirming no `blur` removal happened synchronously with the throw), while the other 17 tests still passed. Restored the fix afterward and reran (18/18 passing). The new test itself asserts on the *same* handler function reference passed to both `addEventListener('blur', ...)` and `removeEventListener('blur', ...)` (not just that some `blur` removal happened at all), to rule out a false pass from the pre-existing unmount-cleanup effect coincidentally also firing during the same test. Also had to work around React's dev-mode event dispatch not letting a synchronous listener throw propagate back out of `fireEvent.click` itself (it resurfaces the error via the window's own `error` event instead, mirroring a real browser's uncaught-exception reporting for a DOM event listener) -- the test captures that via a temporary `window.addEventListener('error', ...)` listener rather than `expect(...).toThrow(...)`.
